"""Startup migrations — collapsed onto the shared library (#2431 T17-9).

The library's ``omnicore_svc_runtime.db.migrate.up`` is a strict superset of
files-svc's former implementation: same goose-CLI-subprocess-under-advisory-
lock control flow, same ``MigrateError``, plus a generic ``roles: Sequence[
RoleCredential]`` rotation list (replacing files-svc's three hardcoded
``_alter_role`` calls) and a hardened ``_alter_role`` (dollar-quoted password
literals + a role-name allowlist, instead of ``''``-doubling).

``with_login`` is always ``True`` for every rotated role in the library,
where files-svc's former code passed ``with_login=False`` for
``files_migrator``/``files_drainer``. This is behavior-preserving here:
both roles are already created ``LOGIN BYPASSRLS`` (migrations/
00011_migrator_role.sql, 00022_drainer_role.sql), so re-asserting ``WITH
LOGIN PASSWORD`` on rotation changes only the password, not the LOGIN/
BYPASSRLS attributes — Postgres only touches attributes explicitly named in
an ``ALTER ROLE`` statement.

files-svc still rotates all three roles — ``files_app``, ``files_migrator``,
and ``files_drainer`` — via the ``roles=`` tuple built below.
``files_migrate`` (the separate NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS DDL role from
migrations/00001_init_schema.sql) is not rotated here, matching
pre-collapse behavior — it was never in the rotation list.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.migrate import MigrateError, RoleCredential
from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.migrate import up as _lib_up

from files_svc.config import GOOSE_TABLE


async def up(
    *,
    admin_dsn: str,
    migrations_dir: Path,
    app_password: str,
    migrator_password: str,
    drainer_password: str = "",
) -> None:
    """Apply all pending migrations + provision app/migrator/drainer roles.

    Thin, files-svc-shaped wrapper over the library's generic ``up()`` so
    ``main.py``'s call site (keyword args per role) doesn't need to change.
    """
    await _lib_up(
        admin_dsn=admin_dsn,
        migrations_dir=migrations_dir,
        goose_table=GOOSE_TABLE,
        service="files-svc",
        roles=(
            RoleCredential(role="files_app", password=app_password),
            RoleCredential(role="files_migrator", password=migrator_password),
            RoleCredential(role="files_drainer", password=drainer_password),
        ),
    )
    # NOTE: no per-role handling after this call. `_lib_up` already warns on an
    # empty password ("no password supplied — leaving role unusable", tagged
    # with the role) and ALTERs the role otherwise, for every credential in
    # `roles` — files_drainer included.
    #
    # A hand-rolled `if not drainer_password: ... else: await _alter_role(...)`
    # block used to sit here, left behind when this module became a thin
    # wrapper. It referenced `_logger` and `_alter_role`, which live in the
    # library and were never imported here, so ruff flagged both as F821
    # undefined names — meaning the `else` branch would have raised NameError
    # the first time a drainer password WAS supplied. Dead and duplicative:
    # removed rather than re-imported.


__all__ = ["MigrateError", "up"]

"""asyncpg-based Postgres pool wrapper — collapsed onto the shared library
(#2431 T17-9).

The library's ``omnicore_svc_runtime.db.pool`` is a strict superset of
files-svc's former implementation: same ``Pool`` dataclass shape
(``app``/``migrator``/``drainer``), same ``with_drain()``/``close()``/
``create_pool()`` signatures, plus an optional ``actor`` kwarg on
``with_org(org_id, actor="")`` that files-svc doesn't pass (files-svc's own
per-request scoping goes through ``db.repo.Repo.with_org()``, which acquires
directly from ``pool.app`` and is untouched by this collapse).

Verified after collapsing: ``Pool.migrator`` stays strictly NOBYPASSRLS/
DDL-only, and the outbox drainer (``events/outbox.py``) still drains through
``Pool.with_drain()`` -> the dedicated BYPASSRLS ``files_drainer`` role
(migrations/00023_drainer_role.sql), never through ``migrator``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from omnicore_svc_runtime.db.pool import Pool, create_pool

__all__ = ["Pool", "create_pool"]

"""SQL constants used by files-svc handlers.

Centralized here so query strings are reusable across handlers + tests
and easy to grep when schema changes.
"""

# --- entity_types ---

LIST_ENTITY_TYPES = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, name, description, color, icon, created_at,
           legacy_id
    FROM files.entity_types
    WHERE ($1::boolean OR org_id IS NOT NULL)
    ORDER BY id
"""

GET_ENTITY_TYPE = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, name, description, color, icon, created_at,
           legacy_id
    FROM files.entity_types
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
"""

# --- relationship_types ---

LIST_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, name, description, is_directed, created_at,
           legacy_id
    FROM files.relationship_types
    WHERE ($1::boolean OR org_id IS NOT NULL)
    ORDER BY id
"""

GET_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, name, description, is_directed, created_at,
           legacy_id
    FROM files.relationship_types
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
"""

# --- corpora ---

INSERT_CORPUS = """
    INSERT INTO files.corpora (id, org_id, name, description, visibility, created_by)
    VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3, $4, $5::files.corpus_visibility, $6::uuid)
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, name, description, visibility::text, created_by::text,
              created_at, legacy_id, is_personal_inbox
"""

# Visibility predicate: TEAM corpora are visible to everyone in the org;
# PRIVATE corpora are visible only to their creator. The org-isolation
# filter still comes from RLS (org_id). NULLIF guards against the empty
# string set_config writes when no user is bound to the tx — without it
# the ::uuid cast on '' raises invalid_text_representation.
# Reused verbatim in GET_CORPUS / LIST_CORPORA / UPDATE_CORPUS /
# DELETE_CORPUS so the access rule has exactly one definition.
_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE = """\
(
    visibility = 'TEAM'
    OR created_by = NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '')::uuid
)"""

# S608 (Possible SQL injection): these queries interpolate a module-level
# constant SQL fragment (_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE), not user input. All
# user-supplied values still flow through asyncpg $N parameters. Ruff
# flags f-string SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE conservatively — explicit noqa here.
GET_CORPUS = f"""
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, name, description, visibility::text, created_by::text,
           created_at, legacy_id, is_personal_inbox
    FROM files.corpora
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
      AND {_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE}
"""

LIST_CORPORA = f"""
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, name, description, visibility::text, created_by::text,
           created_at, legacy_id, is_personal_inbox
    FROM files.corpora
    WHERE id > $1::uuid
      AND {_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE}
    ORDER BY id
    LIMIT $2
"""

UPDATE_CORPUS = f"""
    UPDATE files.corpora
    SET name        = COALESCE($2, name),
        description = COALESCE($3, description),
        visibility  = COALESCE($4::files.corpus_visibility, visibility)
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
      AND {_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE}
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, name, description, visibility::text, created_by::text,
              created_at, legacy_id, is_personal_inbox
"""  # noqa: S608

DELETE_CORPUS = f"""
    DELETE FROM files.corpora
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
      AND {_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE}
    RETURNING id::text
"""  # noqa: S608

# --- entities ---

INSERT_ENTITY = """
    INSERT INTO files.entities
        (id, org_id, type_id, label, description, properties)
    VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4, $5, $6::jsonb)
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, label, description,
              properties, embedding_id::text, created_at, updated_at, legacy_id
"""

GET_ENTITY = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, label, description,
           properties, embedding_id::text, created_at, updated_at, legacy_id
    FROM files.entities WHERE id = $1::uuid
"""

UPDATE_ENTITY = """
    UPDATE files.entities
    SET label       = COALESCE($2, label),
        description = COALESCE($3, description),
        properties  = COALESCE($4::jsonb, properties),
        updated_at  = now()
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, label, description,
              properties, embedding_id::text, created_at, updated_at, legacy_id
"""

DELETE_ENTITY = """
    DELETE FROM files.entities WHERE id = $1::uuid
    RETURNING id::text
"""

# --- entity_edges ---

INSERT_EDGE = """
    INSERT INTO files.entity_edges
        (id, org_id, type_id, source_id, target_id, properties)
    VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4::uuid, $5::uuid, $6::jsonb)
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, source_id::text, target_id::text,
              properties, created_at, legacy_id
"""

GET_EDGE = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, source_id::text, target_id::text,
           properties, created_at, legacy_id
    FROM files.entity_edges WHERE id = $1::uuid
"""

DELETE_EDGE = """
    DELETE FROM files.entity_edges WHERE id = $1::uuid
    RETURNING id::text
"""

# Audit-log scan — newest first, scoped to an action prefix and a target_id.
# event_outbox.payload is a serialized AuditEvent proto; the application
# decodes it and filters by target_id in-process. The subject filter
# narrows the scan to audit envelopes emitted by files-svc.
SELECT_OUTBOX_BY_SUBJECT_PREFIX = """
    SELECT id, payload, created_at
      FROM files.event_outbox
     WHERE subject LIKE $1::text
     ORDER BY id DESC
     LIMIT $2::int
"""

# Update edge type_id and/or properties. NULL args mean "unchanged" via COALESCE.
# Source and target are immutable for the lifetime of an edge.
UPDATE_EDGE = """
    UPDATE files.entity_edges
       SET type_id    = COALESCE($2::uuid, type_id),
           properties = COALESCE($3::jsonb, properties)
     WHERE id = $1::uuid
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, source_id::text, target_id::text,
              properties, created_at, legacy_id
"""

# --- search ---

# Trigram-similarity search on label, optional type-id filter via array overlap.
# `$1::text` = query string, `$2::uuid[]` = optional type filter (NULL = all),
# `$3::int` = limit. Returns ranked entities best-match first.
# RLS scopes the row set to the current org via the connection-level GUC.
SEARCH_ENTITIES_TEXT = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, label, description,
           properties, embedding_id::text, created_at, updated_at, legacy_id,
           similarity(label, $1::text) AS score
    FROM files.entities
    WHERE label % $1::text
      AND ($2::uuid[] IS NULL OR type_id = ANY($2::uuid[]))
    ORDER BY score DESC, label ASC
    LIMIT $3::int
"""

# Recursive seed-fanout: walks the undirected graph from $1::uuid up to depth 2
# and returns entities ranked by inverse distance. Used when seed_entity_id is
# set on SearchRequest. $2::uuid[] = optional type filter, $3::int = limit.
SEARCH_ENTITIES_SEED_FANOUT = """
    WITH RECURSIVE walk(entity_id, depth) AS (
        SELECT $1::uuid AS entity_id, 0 AS depth
        UNION
        SELECT CASE WHEN ee.source_id = w.entity_id THEN ee.target_id
                    ELSE ee.source_id END AS entity_id,
               w.depth + 1 AS depth
        FROM walk w
        JOIN files.entity_edges ee
          ON (ee.source_id = w.entity_id OR ee.target_id = w.entity_id)
        WHERE w.depth < 2
    )
    SELECT e.id::text, e.org_id::text, e.type_id::text, e.label, e.description,
           e.properties, e.embedding_id::text, e.created_at, e.updated_at,
           e.legacy_id,
           (1.0 / (1 + min(w.depth)))::real AS score
    FROM walk w
    JOIN files.entities e ON e.id = w.entity_id
    WHERE w.entity_id <> $1::uuid
      AND ($2::uuid[] IS NULL OR e.type_id = ANY($2::uuid[]))
    GROUP BY e.id, e.org_id, e.type_id, e.label, e.description, e.properties,
             e.embedding_id, e.created_at, e.updated_at, e.legacy_id
    ORDER BY score DESC, e.label ASC
    LIMIT $3::int
"""

# --- neighborhood (EdgeService.Neighborhood) ---

# Returns the seed entity, all entities within `$2::int` hops, and every edge
# connecting any pair within that vertex set. $3::uuid[] = optional edge-type
# filter (NULL = all edge types), $4::uuid[] = optional entity-type filter
# (NULL = all entity types), $5::int = max nodes returned (excluding seed).
NEIGHBORHOOD_SUBGRAPH = """
    WITH RECURSIVE walk(entity_id, depth) AS (
        SELECT $1::uuid AS entity_id, 0 AS depth
        UNION
        SELECT CASE WHEN ee.source_id = w.entity_id THEN ee.target_id
                    ELSE ee.source_id END AS entity_id,
               w.depth + 1 AS depth
        FROM walk w
        JOIN files.entity_edges ee
          ON (ee.source_id = w.entity_id OR ee.target_id = w.entity_id)
         AND ($3::uuid[] IS NULL OR ee.type_id = ANY($3::uuid[]))
        WHERE w.depth < $2::int
    ),
    node_set AS (
        SELECT entity_id, min(depth) AS depth
        FROM walk
        GROUP BY entity_id
    ),
    filtered_nodes AS (
        SELECT n.entity_id, n.depth
        FROM node_set n
        JOIN files.entities e ON e.id = n.entity_id
        WHERE ($4::uuid[] IS NULL OR e.type_id = ANY($4::uuid[]) OR n.depth = 0)
        ORDER BY n.depth ASC, e.label ASC
        LIMIT ($5::int + 1)
    ),
    subgraph_edges AS (
        SELECT ee.id::text AS id, ee.org_id::text AS org_id,
               ee.type_id::text AS type_id, ee.source_id::text AS source_id,
               ee.target_id::text AS target_id, ee.properties,
               ee.created_at, ee.legacy_id
        FROM files.entity_edges ee
        WHERE ee.source_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM filtered_nodes)
          AND ee.target_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM filtered_nodes)
          AND ($3::uuid[] IS NULL OR ee.type_id = ANY($3::uuid[]))
    )
    SELECT
        (
            SELECT row_to_json(seed_row)
            FROM (
                SELECT id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, label, description,
                       properties, embedding_id::text, created_at, updated_at,
                       legacy_id
                FROM files.entities
                WHERE id = $1::uuid
            ) seed_row
        ) AS seed,
        COALESCE(
            (
                SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(ent_row))
                FROM (
                    SELECT e.id::text, e.org_id::text, e.type_id::text, e.label,
                           e.description, e.properties, e.embedding_id::text,
                           e.created_at, e.updated_at, e.legacy_id, fn.depth
                    FROM filtered_nodes fn
                    JOIN files.entities e ON e.id = fn.entity_id
                    WHERE fn.depth > 0
                    ORDER BY fn.depth ASC, e.label ASC
                ) ent_row
            ),
            '[]'::json
        ) AS entities,
        COALESCE(
            (SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(subgraph_edges)) FROM subgraph_edges),
            '[]'::json
        ) AS edges
"""

# --- corpus_entities (M:N membership) ---

# Idempotent insert: if the same (corpus_id, entity_id) is added twice,
# the PRIMARY KEY violation becomes a no-op via ON CONFLICT.
INSERT_CORPUS_ENTITY = """
    INSERT INTO files.corpus_entities (org_id, corpus_id, entity_id)
    VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid)
    ON CONFLICT (corpus_id, entity_id) DO NOTHING
"""

# --- corpus subgraph (CorpusService.ListSubgraph) ---

# Page entity ids in a corpus by id ASC, $2::int = limit, $3::uuid =
# pagination cursor (empty UUID for first page). RLS scopes by org_id.
LIST_CORPUS_ENTITY_IDS = """
    SELECT ce.entity_id::text AS id
    FROM files.corpus_entities ce
    WHERE ce.corpus_id = $1::uuid
      AND ce.entity_id > $3::uuid
    ORDER BY ce.entity_id ASC
    LIMIT $2::int
"""

# Fetch full entity rows by id list. Mirrors GET_ENTITY but takes an array.
LIST_ENTITIES_BY_IDS = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, label, description,
           properties, embedding_id::text, created_at, updated_at, legacy_id
    FROM files.entities
    WHERE id = ANY($1::uuid[])
    ORDER BY id ASC
"""

# Edges where BOTH endpoints are in the supplied id list. Used by the
# canvas-bootstrap RPC so the MFE can render without follow-up Neighborhood
# calls per node.
LIST_EDGES_WITHIN_SET = """
    SELECT id::text, org_id::text, type_id::text, source_id::text, target_id::text,
           properties, created_at, legacy_id
    FROM files.entity_edges
    WHERE source_id = ANY($1::uuid[])
      AND target_id = ANY($1::uuid[])
    ORDER BY id ASC
"""

# --- documents ---

# FK-only insert — no corpus-visibility check at the DB layer. Any same-org
# member who guesses/enumerates a victim's PRIVATE corpus_id could otherwise
# plant a document (and trigger a real ingest job) inside it. Callers MUST
# pre-check corpus visibility (see CrudMixin.Upload, which fetches GET_CORPUS
# before this INSERT — same defense-in-depth pattern CorpusService.
# ListSubgraph uses at corpus.py:228, and INSERT_FOLDER above).
INSERT_DOCUMENT = """
    INSERT INTO files.documents
        (id, org_id, corpus_id, folder_id, filename, mime_type,
         size_bytes, minio_object, uploaded_by)
    VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, $3::uuid, $4::uuid, $5, $6,
            $7::bigint, $8, $9::uuid)
    RETURNING id::text, org_id::text, corpus_id::text, folder_id::text,
              filename, mime_type, size_bytes, minio_object,
              uploaded_by::text, uploaded_at, legacy_id
"""

# Corpus-visibility gate: files.documents RLS is org-scoped ONLY, so a
# same-org caller who supplies (or guesses) another user's document UUID
# would otherwise read that document's metadata AND — via GetRawFile, which
# shares this query — its raw bytes, even when the owning corpus is
# PRIVATE (e.g. a personal-inbox corpus). The EXISTS subquery re-applies
# the same _CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE the corpus reads enforce (TEAM, or
# PRIVATE owned by the current user), so a single-document Get/GetRawFile
# is gated exactly like reading the corpus itself (mirrors
# LIST_DOCUMENTS_BY_CORPUS). Unqualified visibility/created_by resolve to
# files.corpora c (the only relation in the subquery scope); d.corpus_id
# is the correlation.
GET_DOCUMENT = f"""
    SELECT d.id::text, d.org_id::text, d.corpus_id::text,
           d.folder_id::text, d.filename, d.mime_type, d.size_bytes,
           d.minio_object, d.uploaded_by::text, d.uploaded_at,
           d.legacy_id, d.known_type,
           COALESCE(j.status::text, '') AS ingest_status
    FROM files.documents d
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT status
        FROM files.ingest_jobs ij
        WHERE ij.document_id = d.id
        ORDER BY ij.created_at DESC
        LIMIT 1
    ) j ON TRUE
    WHERE d.id = $1::uuid
      AND d.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM files.corpora c
          WHERE c.id = d.corpus_id
            AND {_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE}
      )
"""  # noqa: S608

# Ungated single-document read for the TRUSTED ingest worker path ONLY.
#
# This restores the pre-IDOR-fix GET_DOCUMENT semantics (id + active-only,
# NO corpus-visibility EXISTS gate). The worker opens its tx with
# `with_org(org_id=…, service_account="files-svc-worker")` and NO user_id,
# so `app.current_user_id` is empty and the _CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE would
# reject every PRIVATE / personal-inbox document — stranding it in
# status='failed' error='document not found'. The worker is already
# org-isolated by RLS and never serves these bytes to a caller, so the
# user-scoped visibility gate does not apply to it. Client-facing reads
# (DocumentService.Get / GetRawFile / Copy) MUST keep using the gated
# GET_DOCUMENT above.
GET_DOCUMENT_FOR_INGEST = """
    SELECT d.id::text, d.org_id::text, d.corpus_id::text,
           d.folder_id::text, d.filename, d.mime_type, d.size_bytes,
           d.minio_object, d.uploaded_by::text, d.uploaded_at,
           d.legacy_id
    FROM files.documents d
    WHERE d.id = $1::uuid
      AND d.deleted_at IS NULL
"""

# Stamp the known-type classification the ingest worker's parse phase read
# out of the document's own bytes (#256). Written in the SAME transaction as
# the parsed chunks, so the classification and the text it was derived from
# land together — a worker that dies between them leaves the job 'parsing'
# and JetStream redelivers the whole phase.
#
# $2 is NULL for "not a known type", which is the overwhelmingly common
# case. Writing NULL rather than skipping the UPDATE matters on RETRY: a
# failed job that is redelivered after the document was REPLACED at the same
# object key must be able to clear a stale classification, not inherit one.
#
# INTENTIONALLY UNGATED, like GET_DOCUMENT_FOR_INGEST above: the worker runs
# under its own org-scoped tx and there is no user whose corpus visibility
# could be consulted. The id comes from the ingest job's own document_id,
# never from a caller.
# files-query-lint: allow-trash-state-agnostic
STAMP_DOCUMENT_KNOWN_TYPE = """
    UPDATE files.documents
       SET known_type = $2::text
     WHERE id = $1::uuid
"""

# folder_id filter ($4) is bypassed entirely when $5 (all_folders) is true:
#   $5 = true               → every document in the corpus (folder_id ignored)
#   $5 = false, $4 IS NULL  → corpus-root documents (folder_id IS NULL)
#   $5 = false, $4 NOT NULL → documents in that specific folder
#
# ingest_status is sourced from the latest files.ingest_jobs row for
# each document (LEFT JOIN LATERAL keeps the doc visible even when no
# ingest_job exists, e.g. legacy migrator-imported rows).
#
# Corpus-visibility gate: files.documents RLS is org-scoped ONLY, so a
# same-org caller who supplies another user's PRIVATE (e.g. personal-inbox)
# corpus_id would otherwise read every document in it — and all_folders=true
# turns that into a whole-corpus leak. The EXISTS subquery re-applies the same
# _CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE the corpus reads enforce (TEAM, or PRIVATE owned by
# the current user), so listing documents is gated exactly like reading the
# corpus itself. Unqualified visibility/created_by resolve to files.corpora c
# (the only relation in the subquery scope); d.corpus_id is the correlation.
LIST_DOCUMENTS_BY_CORPUS = f"""
    SELECT d.id::text, d.org_id::text, d.corpus_id::text,
           d.folder_id::text, d.filename, d.mime_type, d.size_bytes,
           d.minio_object, d.uploaded_by::text, d.uploaded_at,
           d.legacy_id, d.known_type,
           COALESCE(j.status::text, '') AS ingest_status
    FROM files.documents d
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT status
        FROM files.ingest_jobs ij
        WHERE ij.document_id = d.id
        ORDER BY ij.created_at DESC
        LIMIT 1
    ) j ON TRUE
    WHERE d.corpus_id = $1::uuid
      AND d.id > $2::uuid
      AND d.deleted_at IS NULL

# Resolve "/<parent_name>/<…>/<self_name>" from a folder_id for the
# deleted_from_folder_path snapshot at trash time. Returns '' if NULL.
#
# INTENTIONALLY UNGATED: the seed `folder_id` is never caller input — it comes
# from `existing["folder_id"]` on the already-gated GET_DOCUMENT_BY_ID row in
# handlers/document/_trash.py, so corpus visibility was enforced upstream in the
# same tx. Gating the seed again would be redundant; RLS org-isolation applies
# via the tx's org_id GUC.
RESOLVE_FOLDER_PATH = """
    WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
        SELECT id, parent_folder_id, name, 1 AS depth
        FROM files.folders WHERE id = $1::uuid
        UNION ALL
        SELECT f.id, f.parent_folder_id, f.name, c.depth + 1
        FROM files.folders f JOIN chain c ON f.id = c.parent_folder_id
    )
    SELECT '/' || string_agg(name, '/' ORDER BY depth DESC) AS path
    FROM chain
"""

"""Repo layer — owns Pool, audit-key provider, and audit-emission flow.

Each `with_org` context manager opens a transaction, sets the RLS GUC,
and yields a RepoTx whose `emit_audit_event` method handles the full
audit-emission chain:

    1. Query last row_hash (FOR UPDATE) from files.event_outbox.
    2. Build AuditEvent proto with standard fields.
    3. ChainEvent stamps prev_row_hash + key_id + row_hash.
    4. INSERT into files.event_outbox (within same tx).

This mirrors services/identity-svc/internal/repo/repo.go's
emitUserInvited flow exactly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import asyncpg

from files_svc.audit.chain import chain_event
from files_svc.audit.emit import build_audit_event, insert_outbox, last_row_hash
from files_svc.audit.keys_env import EnvKeyProvider
from files_svc.audit.keys_vault import VaultKeyProvider
from files_svc.db.pool import Pool

KeyProvider = EnvKeyProvider | VaultKeyProvider


@dataclass(slots=True)
class RepoTx:
    """Transaction context yielded by Repo.with_org. Owns the connection
    + the audit-emission flow for the duration of the transaction."""

    conn: asyncpg.Connection
    _keys: KeyProvider
    _org_id: str
    _user_id: str
    _service_account: str
    _request_id: str

    async def emit_audit_event(
        self,
        *,
        action: str,
        target_type: str,
        target_id: str,
        payload: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Emit an audit event within the open transaction.

        Action format: "files.<entity>.<verb>" (e.g. "files.corpus.created").
        Subject derived: "audit.files.<entity>_<verb>".
        """
        prev = await last_row_hash(self.conn, self._org_id)
        ev = build_audit_event(
            action=action,
            target_type=target_type,
            target_id=target_id,
            payload_dict=payload,
            org_id=self._org_id,
            user_id=self._user_id,
            service_account=self._service_account,
            request_id=self._request_id,
        )
        key_id, key = self._keys.active()
        chain_event(ev, prev=prev, key_id=key_id, key=key)
        # action="files.corpus.created" → subject="audit.files.corpus_created"
        suffix = action.removeprefix("files.").replace(".", "_")
        subject = f"audit.files.{suffix}"
        await insert_outbox(self.conn, subject, ev)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Repo:
    """Owns Pool + audit keys; provides per-request transaction scope."""

    pool: Pool
    keys: KeyProvider

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def with_org(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        user_id: str = "",
        service_account: str = "",
        request_id: str = "",
    ) -> AsyncIterator[RepoTx]:
        """Acquire connection, BEGIN, set RLS GUC, yield RepoTx, COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

        Exactly one of user_id or service_account must be set; emit_audit_event
        will raise ValueError otherwise.
        """
        async with self.pool.app.acquire() as conn:
            tx = conn.transaction()
            await tx.start()
            try:
                # `SET LOCAL` doesn't accept $N params; set_config(..., true)
                # is the equivalent transaction-local GUC and does.
                await conn.execute(
                    "SELECT set_config('app.current_org_id', $1, true)",
                    org_id,
                )
                # current_user_id is read by visibility predicates (e.g.
                # private corpora are only visible to created_by). Service
                # accounts pass an empty user_id; queries that require an
                # owner check treat empty as "not the owner" — i.e. they
                # only see TEAM rows.
                await conn.execute(
                    "SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', $1, true)",
                    user_id,
                )
                yield RepoTx(
                    conn=conn,
                    _keys=self.keys,
                    _org_id=org_id,
                    _user_id=user_id,
                    _service_account=service_account,
                    _request_id=request_id,
                )
            except BaseException:
                await tx.rollback()
                raise
            else:
                await tx.commit()

# the whole corpus's trash today regardless of ownership, which is the
# existing/expected admin-override behavior. This stays open until the
# x-org-role azp-trust gap is fixed (blocker ticket to be filed separately).

           d.folder_id::text, d.filename, d.mime_type, d.size_bytes,

    WHERE d.corpus_id = $1::uuid
      AND d.deleted_at IS NOT NULL
      AND (d.deleted_at, d.id) < ($2::timestamptz, $3::uuid)
    ORDER BY d.deleted_at DESC, d.id DESC
    LIMIT $4::int

    FROM files.documents

"""

# Resolve "/<parent_name>/<…>/<self_name>" from a folder_id for the
# deleted_from_folder_path snapshot at trash time. Returns '' if NULL.
#
# INTENTIONALLY UNGATED: the seed `folder_id` is never caller input — it comes
# from `existing["folder_id"]` on the already-gated GET_DOCUMENT_BY_ID row in
# handlers/document/_trash.py, so corpus visibility was enforced upstream in the
# same tx. Gating the seed again would be redundant; RLS org-isolation applies
# via the tx's org_id GUC.
RESOLVE_FOLDER_PATH = """
    WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
        SELECT id, parent_folder_id, name, 1 AS depth
        FROM files.folders WHERE id = $1::uuid
        UNION ALL
        SELECT f.id, f.parent_folder_id, f.name, c.depth + 1
        FROM files.folders f JOIN chain c ON f.id = c.parent_folder_id
    )
    SELECT '/' || string_agg(name, '/' ORDER BY depth DESC) AS path
    FROM chain
"""

    FROM files.documents
    WHERE id = $1::uuid
    FOR UPDATE

# rows points at a chunk in the target set — i.e. removing those chunks
# would leave it with no source citation.
ORPHAN_PRE_CHECK = """
    WITH target_chunks AS (
        SELECT unnest($1::uuid[]) AS chunk_id
    ),
    affected_entities AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT ep.entity_id
        FROM files.entity_provenance ep
        WHERE ep.chunk_id IN (SELECT chunk_id FROM target_chunks)
    ),
    orphan_entities AS (
        SELECT ae.entity_id FROM affected_entities ae
        WHERE NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM files.entity_provenance ep2
            WHERE ep2.entity_id = ae.entity_id
              AND ep2.chunk_id NOT IN (SELECT chunk_id FROM target_chunks)
        )
    ),
    affected_edges AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT ep.edge_id
        FROM files.edge_provenance ep
        WHERE ep.chunk_id IN (SELECT chunk_id FROM target_chunks)
    ),
    orphan_edges AS (
        SELECT ae.edge_id FROM affected_edges ae
        WHERE NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM files.edge_provenance ep2
            WHERE ep2.edge_id = ae.edge_id
              AND ep2.chunk_id NOT IN (SELECT chunk_id FROM target_chunks)
        )
    )
    SELECT 'entity'::text AS kind, e.id::text AS id, e.label AS label,
           et.name AS entity_type
    FROM orphan_entities oe
    JOIN files.entities e ON e.id = oe.entity_id
    JOIN files.entity_types et ON et.id = e.type_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'edge'::text AS kind, ed.id::text AS id, rt.name AS label,
           NULL::text AS entity_type
    FROM orphan_edges oeg
    JOIN files.entity_edges ed ON ed.id = oeg.edge_id

"""Repo layer — owns Pool, audit-key provider, and audit-emission flow.

Each `with_org` context manager opens a transaction, sets the RLS GUC,
and yields a RepoTx whose `emit_audit_event` method handles the full
audit-emission chain:

    1. Query last row_hash (FOR UPDATE) from files.event_outbox.
    2. Build AuditEvent proto with standard fields.
    3. ChainEvent stamps prev_row_hash + key_id + row_hash.
    4. INSERT into files.event_outbox (within same tx).

This mirrors services/identity-svc/internal/repo/repo.go's
emitUserInvited flow exactly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import asyncpg

from files_svc.audit.chain import chain_event
from files_svc.audit.emit import build_audit_event, insert_outbox, last_row_hash
from files_svc.audit.keys_env import EnvKeyProvider
from files_svc.audit.keys_vault import VaultKeyProvider
from files_svc.db.pool import Pool

KeyProvider = EnvKeyProvider | VaultKeyProvider


@dataclass(slots=True)
class RepoTx:
    """Transaction context yielded by Repo.with_org. Owns the connection
    + the audit-emission flow for the duration of the transaction."""

    conn: asyncpg.Connection
    _keys: KeyProvider
    _org_id: str
    _user_id: str
    _service_account: str
    _request_id: str

    async def emit_audit_event(
        self,
        *,
        action: str,
        target_type: str,
        target_id: str,
        payload: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Emit an audit event within the open transaction.

        Action format: "files.<entity>.<verb>" (e.g. "files.corpus.created").
        Subject derived: "audit.files.<entity>_<verb>".
        """
        prev = await last_row_hash(self.conn, self._org_id)
        ev = build_audit_event(
            action=action,
            target_type=target_type,
            target_id=target_id,
            payload_dict=payload,
            org_id=self._org_id,
            user_id=self._user_id,
            service_account=self._service_account,
            request_id=self._request_id,
        )
        key_id, key = self._keys.active()
        chain_event(ev, prev=prev, key_id=key_id, key=key)
        # action="files.corpus.created" → subject="audit.files.corpus_created"
        suffix = action.removeprefix("files.").replace(".", "_")
        subject = f"audit.files.{suffix}"
        await insert_outbox(self.conn, subject, ev)


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Repo:
    """Owns Pool + audit keys; provides per-request transaction scope."""

    pool: Pool
    keys: KeyProvider

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def with_org(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        user_id: str = "",
        service_account: str = "",
        request_id: str = "",
    ) -> AsyncIterator[RepoTx]:
        """Acquire connection, BEGIN, set RLS GUC, yield RepoTx, COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

        Exactly one of user_id or service_account must be set; emit_audit_event
        will raise ValueError otherwise.
        """
        async with self.pool.app.acquire() as conn:
            tx = conn.transaction()
            await tx.start()
            try:
                # `SET LOCAL` doesn't accept $N params; set_config(..., true)
                # is the equivalent transaction-local GUC and does.
                await conn.execute(
                    "SELECT set_config('app.current_org_id', $1, true)",
                    org_id,
                )
                # current_user_id is read by visibility predicates (e.g.
                # private corpora are only visible to created_by). Service
                # accounts pass an empty user_id; queries that require an
                # owner check treat empty as "not the owner" — i.e. they
                # only see TEAM rows.
                await conn.execute(
                    "SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', $1, true)",
                    user_id,
                )
                yield RepoTx(
                    conn=conn,
                    _keys=self.keys,
                    _org_id=org_id,
                    _user_id=user_id,
                    _service_account=service_account,
                    _request_id=request_id,
                )
            except BaseException:
                await tx.rollback()
                raise
            else:
                await tx.commit()

If you want to:

- **Regenerate proto stubs (Go/Python/TS)**: `make proto`
- **Regenerate only TS proto stubs**: `make proto-ts`
- **Lint proto**: `make proto-lint`
- **Check proto breaking changes**: `make proto-breaking`
- **Run Go tests for a service**: `cd services/<svc> && go test -short ./...` (or `make <svc>-test`)
- **Run one Go test by name**: `go test -run '^TestName$' ./internal/...`
- **Run Go integration tests**: `go test -tags=integration -run '^TestName$' ./tests/integration/...` (or `make <svc>-test-int`, Docker required)
- **Run all Go modules + coverage file**: `make go-test` (or `make go-test-short` to skip testcontainers)
- **Check Go coverage gate**: `make go-coverage`
- **Tidy Go modules**: `make go-tidy`
- **Vet Go code**: `go vet ./...` (from service dir)
- **Run Vitest for one workspace**: `pnpm test`
- **Watch Vitest (TDD loop)**: `pnpm test:watch`
- **Run one Vitest test by name**: `pnpm test -- --run -t "<name>"`
- **Run Vitest with coverage**: `pnpm test -- --coverage`
- **Recompile Paraglide i18n messages**: `pnpm --filter @omnicore-platform/platform-chrome run compile-messages` (then hand-wire `frontends/platform-chrome/src/paraglide/messages.ts`)
- **Audit i18n locale parity/ICU/glossary**: `npx tsx scripts/i18n-audit.ts`
- **Fast glossary-only i18n check**: `cd frontends/platform-chrome && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/glossary.regression.test.ts`
- **Regenerate Range location-wizard geo shards (offline)**: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts` (network refresh: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts --fetch` first, to repopulate `scripts/geo-sources/`)
- **Lint an MFE**: `pnpm lint`
- **Typecheck an MFE**: `pnpm typecheck`
- **Bring up the whole stack (baked images)**: `make up` (`SCOPE=<vertical>` to limit, `CLEAN=1` to wipe volumes, `BUILD=1` to rebuild images from fresh proto)
- **`make up` never builds two MFE images at once — not even the ones `BUILD=` did not name**: each Vite build takes an 8GB Node heap, so the guarded loop (`_build-guarded`) builds non-MFE images in parallel and MFE images strictly one at a time. That guard used to cover only the `BUILD=`-selected set, while `up`'s final `docker compose up -d` carried no `--no-build` and every locally-built service keeps its `build:` context — so anything `BUILD=` missed and `stack-pin-images.py` could not snapshot (which is *everything* on a machine with no bare `:dev` tags left to snapshot from) was built by **compose** instead, all at once. 11 concurrent Vite builds either die with `ResourceExhausted: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm run build" ... cannot allocate memory` or drives an OOM-kill spiral that wedges the Docker daemon, so `make up` just *hangs* with no error at all. `up` now plans the absent set itself (`platform/scripts/plan-implicit-builds.py`), builds it through the same guard, and passes `--no-build` so any remaining hole fails loudly instead of fanning out. `make dev` deliberately keeps compose's implicit build: its MFE layer is host-side vite servers, not containers, so only service images can be built there. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_build_guarded.py platform/scripts/test_plan_implicit_builds.py -q`.
- **AI backend mode (unified across verticals, `omnicore_svc_runtime.ai`)**: real inference-server litellm/vLLM (over Tailscale) is now the default for `make up`/`make dev` — `AI_DEV_MODE` is unset/false in `.env.example`. `AI_TEST_MODE=true` → StubLLM (deterministic, wins over `AI_DEV_MODE`). `AI_DEV_MODE=true` → local Ollama backend (`platform/compose/ollama.yml`, litellm alias `ollama-dev`). Old per-service flags (`STUDIO_AI_DEV_MODE`, `RANGE_AI_DEV_MODE`, `DIALOGUE_AI_DRAFT_DEV_MODE`) are gone — hard cutover. Per-vertical model pins (`RANGE_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `qwen3.5:9b`; `STUDIO_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss:20b`; `LITELLM_DRAFT_MODEL` for dialogue, default `gpt-oss:20b`) live as env-overridable defaults in `range-svc.yml`/`range-svc-worker.yml`/`studio-svc.yml`/`studio-svc-worker.yml`/`dialogue-svc.yml`/`dialogue-svc-worker.yml`.
- **Boot-time AI reachability probe + offline/force-live escape hatches**: `make up`/`make dev` run a preflight (`platform/scripts/ai-live-probe.py`) before compose starts, checking each in-scope AI-capable vertical's resolved model against the real gateway. Reachable → live mode, printed per-vertical. Unreachable with local Ollama available → loud degraded-fallback banner, never a silent per-call swap. Unreachable with no Ollama → the target fails outright. `OFFLINE=1` (formerly `RANGE_AI_MODE`, now `AI_OFFLINE_MODE`, vertical-scope-agnostic) skips the probe entirely and forces local Ollama — airplane-mode / no-Tailscale case. `REQUIRE_LIVE=1` turns an unreachable gateway into a hard failure instead of a degraded fallback. `STUB=1` means `AI_TEST_MODE=true` (deterministic StubLLM) — it does NOT mean local Ollama; use `OFFLINE=1` for that.
- **Hot-reload dev stack (services + MFEs)**: `make dev` (`SCOPE=` honored)
- **Boot an isolated walled local stack (own compose project, own hostname, one published port)**: `make up STACK=<name>` — needs `*.localhost` to resolve, which works out of the box on macOS (no other OS supported yet). Not seeded automatically: a fresh stack has no users until you also run `make seed STACK=<name>`.
- **Hot-reload a walled local stack**: `make dev STACK=<name>` — the walled overlay is derived from `dev`'s OWN compose file set (never `up`'s), so a scoped `dev` never references a service (e.g. an MFE container) that `dev` itself doesn't bring up, and shell-bff's dev-mode volumes (the `/workspace` bind + Go module/build caches) survive the per-stack mtls rewrite instead of being silently dropped.
- **A bare `make up` in a worktree warns before driving the SHARED stack**: `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME ?= omnicore-platform` is identical in every worktree and is only reassigned inside the `STACK=` block, so `make up` / `dev` / `seed` / `down` / `clean` / `cypress-run` with no `STACK=` drives that ONE project and its volumes from whatever worktree you happen to be in. `up`/`dev`/`seed`/`down`/`clean`/`cypress-*` now print the derived `STACK=<name>` you probably wanted and pause 3s. It is warn-only, never fatal — silence it with `OMNICORE_NO_STACK_WARN=1` (or pass `STACK=platform` to say you meant the shared one). Silent in the primary checkout, which legitimately owns that project.
- **List running local stacks and their URLs**: `make stacks` — the state column is `up` / `down` / `orphaned` / `orphaned-up`. `orphaned` means the worktree that owned the pin no longer exists on disk; `orphaned-up` means that AND it is still live and serving, so its port must not be reused.
- **Drop pins whose worktree is gone**: `make stack-gc` (`DRY=1` to preview). Nothing used to remove a pin except an explicit `release` run from the owning worktree, so a `git worktree remove` left its entry behind forever, holding a name and a port. `gc` deliberately refuses to drop an `orphaned-up` pin — that stack is still serving, and freeing its port would let a second stack claim it.
- **Retire a stack for good**: `make stack-release STACK=<name>` — drops the registry pin, this worktree's generated `.omnicore/` files for it, AND its per-stack image tags. Prefer this over `stack.py release` now that image tags are per-stack, since the bare script cannot clean those up (it owns identity only, no docker).
- **Print one stack's URL**: `make stack-url STACK=<name>`
- **Seed a walled stack's default data**: `make seed STACK=<name>` (same idempotent seed as the primary — 1 org + 1 workspace + 10 role-combo users + 1 range exercise; `make seed` with no `STACK=` seeds the primary)
- **Open psql against a walled stack's postgres**: `make psql STACK=<name>`
- **Publish a walled stack's postgres+nats on two extra host ports for GUI DB clients**: `DB_PORTS=1` (only meaningful with `STACK=<name>`, e.g. `make up STACK=review DB_PORTS=1`)
- **Hot-reload one MFE into a walled stack**: `make <vertical>-mfe-dev-federated STACK=<name>` — routes `/<vertical>-mfe/` through that stack's own ingress to your local vite server instead of the baked image. Safe to run for several MFEs at once in the same stack: each invocation re-reads every OTHER live `--hot` MFE's probed port from `.omnicore/hot-<stack>-*.port` and re-adds it, so starting a second one doesn't 502 the first; the port file is removed automatically when that MFE's dev server exits.
- **Run the cross-stack isolation gate (12 vectors)**: `make stack-isolation-test STACK_A=<name> STACK_B=<name>` (both stacks already up; the unwalled primary's name here is `platform`, e.g. `STACK_A=platform`)
- **Reach a walled stack's admin consoles**: same single published port, different sub-hostnames — `auth.<name>.localhost:<port>` (Keycloak), `grafana.<name>.localhost:<port>`, `minio.<name>.localhost:<port>`, `prom.<name>.localhost:<port>`
- **Reach a walled stack's Vault**: no ingress route and no host port, deliberately — `docker exec` into the stack's vault container (see `make vault-pki-bootstrap`)
- **Provision mTLS PKI for a walled stack**: `make vault-pki-bootstrap STACK=<name>` — writes issued certs to that stack's own `.omnicore/secrets-<name>/mtls` tree (`CA_OUT_DIR`) instead of the shared `platform/secrets/mtls` the unwalled path uses.
- **Force a stack's pinned port to re-probe**: `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py resolve --stack <name> --reprobe` — only needed when something else grabbed the previously-pinned port while the stack was down; a plain `make up STACK=<name>` never re-probes an already-pinned, currently-live port out from under itself.
- **Where stack names/ports are pinned**: `~/.omnicore/stacks.json`, machine-wide (NOT per-worktree) — a stack name becomes a hostname and a compose project, both of which are machine-global, so one registry arbitrates them across every worktree. The generated artifacts (ingress config, walled overlay, per-stack secrets, hot-port files) stay in each worktree's own `.omnicore/`, since they are built from that worktree's source.
- **A stack name belongs to the worktree that created it**: reusing the same `STACK=<name>` from a different worktree is refused, not silently shared — `stack 'x' is owned by a different worktree -- refusing to touch it.` naming both paths. Without this, two worktrees would resolve the same compose project and the second `make up` would recreate the first's containers from its own source, i.e. a reviewer's stack silently serving another branch's code. Pick a different name (`make up STACK=<name>-2`) or release it with `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py release <name>`.
- **Pact broker across stacks**: shared by design, not per-stack — a `STACK=<name>` `pact-publish`/`pact-verify`/`pact-smoke` still targets the ONE broker at `localhost:9292`, same broker CI uses
- **litellm/GPU is NOT shared across walled stacks** (deviation from the design spec's §8, which called for a shared `omnicore-shared` litellm project): each walled stack runs its own ~792 MiB litellm container. The GPU can't be meaningfully partitioned, so a real shared instance is future work; until then, budget ~792 MiB/stack for it specifically, on top of the capacity figures below.
- **Local stack capacity**: one walled stack is ~76 containers behind one published port, ~50-80s to boot. Four stacks running concurrently (305 containers) measured 8.23 GiB of a 23.43 GiB Docker Desktop VM (35%) once idle — idle stacks compress well below their boot-time peak, so the ~4.2 GiB/stack figure in the design spec (measured immediately post-boot) overstates steady state.
- **EVERY locally-built image is tagged per stack, not just shell-mfe**: a walled stack runs `omnicore-platform/<svc>:<tag>-<name>` (e.g. `range-svc:dev-review`, and `:dev-hotreload-review` under `make dev`); shell-mfe keeps its own `:walled-<name>`. Before this, the compose project, hostname, port, mTLS tree and litellm keys were all per-stack but the ~67 `image: ...:dev` tags were machine-global, so ANY worktree's `make up STACK=<x> BUILD=...` replaced the image a different, still-running stack would resolve on its next container recreate — that stack then silently served another branch's code, and all 11 isolation vectors still passed because every one of them tested *runtime* isolation. `up`/`dev` now snapshot the tags via `docker tag` (metadata only, no rebuild) just before `up -d`; see `platform/scripts/stack-pin-images.py`.
- **A pinned stack does NOT pick up a newer `:dev` on restart — that's the point**: the snapshot is sticky, so a plain `make up STACK=<name>` keeps serving the image IDs it was pinned to even after another worktree rebuilds `:dev`. To deliberately adopt the current build, pass `REPIN=1` (`make up STACK=<name> REPIN=1`). A `BUILD=` run always builds straight into the per-stack tag, so it needs no `REPIN`.
- **Vector 12 is image provenance**: it fails a stack whose containers sit on a machine-global (unsuffixed) tag, and separately flags a container whose running image ID no longer matches what its own tag resolves to — i.e. the tag was rebuilt underneath a live container. The unwalled `platform` stack is SKIPPED there, since it legitimately owns the bare `:dev` tags.
- **Bring up infra only (for running services/tests by hand)**: `make infra`
- **Check infra health**: `make infra-test`
- **Tear the stack down**: `make down` / `make clean` (clean deletes volumes)
- **Validate a compose file**: `docker compose --env-file .env -f platform/compose/infra.yml -f platform/compose/infra.dev.yml -f platform/compose/<svc>.yml config > /dev/null`
- **One-time init + per-restart unseal for server-mode Vault**: `make vault-init` (no-op against dev-mode Vault; run after every restart of a non-dev Vault, including `infra-prod`)
- **Provision mTLS PKI locally**: `make vault-pki-bootstrap`

- **Run the k6 load-test harness**: `make load-test` (`SUITE=<name>`, default `smoke`; requires a running stack)
- **EVERY gate locally, in dependency order (~1h)**: `make full-local-pass` — the union of `pr-preflight`, the gates it doesn't mirror (actionlint, markdownlint, gitleaks, drift guard, files-query-lint, make-flags, cve-report, compose-isolation), CI's multi-module Go coverage MERGE gate, a real image build, a pact round-trip, and every Cypress spec against ONE stack boot. Since PR CI now runs only the cheap class, this is what gives you the signal `develop` would have. - **Fast pre-PR gate (no Docker) — mirrors CI at changed scope**: `make pr-preflight` — runs CI's unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands for the files you changed (via `ci-changed-scope.py`), so a green run predicts green CI for those gates without spending Actions minutes. `INT=1` adds testcontainer integration. - **Advisory full-stack Cypress dress rehearsal for one vertical**: `make pr-preflight-e2e SCOPE=<vertical>` (needs Node 20 + Chrome + Docker). - **Pre-push hook (automatic)**: `.husky/pre-push` runs a fast changed-scope smoke (Go `-short`, MFE typecheck/lint/vitest, Python `ruff`) before every push. Bypass once with `git push --no-verify` or `SKIP_PREPUSH=1`; CI still gates.
- **Read a pre-push failure you scrolled past**: the run is logged to `"$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)"/pre-push.log`, per-worktree, replaced each run; per-lane output sits in the sibling `pre-push-lanes/`. A failing run also replays each failing lane's tail after the `FAILED:` roster, so nothing is lost to scrollback. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_prepush_hook.py -q`.
- **Start a GitHub issue in its own worktree**: `./scripts/github/create-issue-branch.sh <issue> --worktree --type <type> <section>/<summary>` — creates the branch under `.worktrees/<branch>` via `make worktree` (so `.husky/_` is generated and hooks are live) and leaves the calling tree on its current branch. The epic branch is resolved to a ref, never checked out — a branch checked out in one worktree can't be checked out in another. Tests: `python3 -m pytest scripts/github/test_create_issue_branch.py -q`.
- **See every build/test/stack target**: `make help`

## CI runs on the promotion to `develop`, not on the PR

Everything that costs GitHub Actions minutes now fires on `push` to `develop`,
the promotion of `main`: Go `-race` + coverage gate, frontend unit + coverage,
Python *integration* (testcontainers), migration lint, i18n, pact, proto
compatibility, image build/sign/verify, and all eight Cypress lanes.

**Python lint/typecheck/unit is the exception, as of #2811.** `python-test.yml`
had no `pull_request` trigger at all, so no ruff, `mypy --strict` or pytest run
touched a PR *or* the merge to `main` — a Python regression could not surface
before the promotion. Its cheap legs (`py lint`, `lint + typecheck + unit`,
`lint + typecheck (shared python libs)`) now run on PRs; they were already on
`ubuntu-24-arm-2core` and the `changes` job scopes both matrices to the services
a PR touches. The heavy `integration (<svc>)` matrix stays promotion-only —
that is the half the original cost argument was about.

The cheap class still runs on the PR, again on the merge commit to `main`, and
again on the promotion to `develop`. It runs on `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` — a
GitHub-hosted ARM64 larger runner: billed, but at the ARM rate, out of its own
concurrency pool rather than the plan's 60 standard slots, and seconds-to-a-few-
minutes per job. So `main` keeps per-merge signal for these:

| Check | Workflow | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown lint, Compose config validation, Keycloak realm-export lint, Branch-protection doc sync, Load-harness lib tests | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Secret Scan (gitleaks) | `secret-scan.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Action Lint | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Go Vuln Scan (govulncheck) | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| golangci-lint (new-issues-only) | `go-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, **PR only** |
| py lint / lint + typecheck + unit (`<svc>`), lint + typecheck (shared python libs) | `python-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (scoped to changed services; `integration (<svc>)` stays develop-only) |
| No duplicate Prometheus metrics in a boot graph | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image | `sign-and-verify.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (that workflow has no `main` trigger) |
| go test -short (every changed module) | `go-test.yml` | self-hosted, **push to `main` only** |

### The self-hosted mac fleet no longer runs anything on a PR

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to
`github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'` — NOT to
`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

Consequences worth internalizing:

- **A required check that reports `skipped` counts as PASSED.** `go test +
  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without
  running anything. Do not read it as signal, and do not re-add it to the `main`
  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example
  and deliberately so: #2369 un-skipped it precisely because a skipped required
  check proved nothing, so it really does run on every PR.
- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**
  It runs CI's own unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands at the
  changed scope. `INT=1` adds the testcontainer integration suites — still worth
  running, since Python integration remains promotion-only. If it isn't green
  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the
  complete picture — including image builds, pact, and every Cypress spec —
  `make full-local-pass` chains every gate in dependency order.
- **`main` catches the cheap class, `develop` catches the rest.** A lint,
  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**
  `prometheus_client`'s registry is process-global, so a second registration of
  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter
  catches it (#2811's arming commit touched none of the seven services it broke).
  `platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py` walks every service's boot
  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with
  `python3 platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py`.
- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
  `git log --oneline <last-good-develop>..develop`, and prefer promoting often
  so that range stays short.

## Testing policy — Cypress e2e

Cypress UI e2e rides in the feature branch. Any PR that adds or changes a user-facing surface owes a spec under `frontends/cypress/cypress/e2e/<vertical>/`, landed in the same branch — as does any change to login, session, invite, or org-role gating, UI diff or not. Backend-only PRs (proto, migration, service handler, BFF route with no UI consumer) don't.

Ownership is split by file, not by team:

- **Feature dev owns:** the spec files themselves, and `support/selectors.ts`.
- **QA/QC-stewarded:** the shared foundation — `cypress.config.ts`, `support/{e2e,commands,personas}.ts`, `tasks/**`, `fixtures/personas.json`.

Two things that bite:

- A spec absent from a workflow's `--spec` list did not run. Wiring it into the relevant GitHub workflow is part of authoring the spec — check that the workflow actually seeds the state the spec needs.
- `e2e.yml` is non-required and posts no check, so a green PR is not evidence a spec ran. Verify locally against `make up`.

# Frontend design system guardrails

- Per `tdd-react` on `tailwind.preset.ts` as the source of truth for `cog-*`: an
  undefined token emits no CSS and is silently invisible, not an error. This branch
  found 52 phantom tokens across 233 occurrences, including 3 passing tests that
  asserted classes rendering nothing. Grep the preset before using any `cog-*` class
  — a test asserting an undefined class is not a safety net.
- **Never inline raw hex or arbitrary Tailwind values** (`text-[#fff]`,
  `border-[1.5px]`) at a call site — define a token in the preset instead.
- **Bare numeric spacing/size utilities are banned** (`p-4`, `gap-6`, `min-h-11`) in
  favor of named `cog-*` rungs. For hit targets specifically, use `min-h-tap` /
  `min-w-tap` (44px) — never `min-h-11`.
- **WCAG 2.5.8 hit areas:** don't enlarge the visible box to hit 44×44. Move the
  drawn box into an inner `aria-hidden` span at its original size, and put the tap
  rungs on the interactive element wrapping it. Applied 7x this branch — follow the
  established pattern rather than inventing a new one.
- **Any new axis added to `tailwind.preset.ts`'s `theme.extend` must be registered in
  `frontends/ui/src/lib/cn.ts`'s `extendTailwindMerge` config.** An unregistered axis
  makes `tailwind-merge` silently DELETE one of two conflicting classes — 5 live
  defects found this branch from exactly this (`text-heading-md`, `bg-cog-ai`,
  `shadow-cog-e1`, `border-field`, letterSpacing). The `CN_axis_parity` rule in
  `platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs` gates it.
- **`Design parity` (`platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs --ci`) is PR-blocking.**
  Its counts are ratchets — they may only go down, never up. A matcher change
  requires re-running with `--update` in the same PR, so the rule diff and the count
  diff review together.
- Test process for any change here: see the `tdd-react` skill.

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to

`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without

  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example

- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**

  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the

  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**

  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter

  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with

- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
